accuracy.evidence: Rule checked against English Appendix 1 (Years 3–4, possessive apostrophe with plural words: 'The apostrophe is placed after the plural form of the word; -s is not added if the plural already ends in -s, but is added if the plural does not end in -s (i.e. is an irregular plural – e.g. children's)') and Appendix 2 Year 4 (girls', boys'). Every lab answer follows it: plus() writes girls', teachers', babies' and cat's, horse's; NOS gives children's, women's, men's, mice's. No example relies on the contested singular-ending-in-s cases (James's / James'), so nothing taught is open to dispute. The adult text places singular possession in Year 2 and plural possession in Year 4 as the curriculum does.

misconceptions.evidence: The lab targets the documented Year 3–5 errors: singular form for several owners (count step: 'girl's means one girl. The picture shows 3 girls'; PROOF 'boy's' for three boys), the double s (PROOF girls's), invented plurals childrens'/womens'/mices' (NOS s' tile, PROOF childrens', challenge q2 and q5), the missing mark (PROOF womens race), the greengrocer's apostrophe on a plain plural (PROOF Both cat's, challenge q4, m3), and misreading 'the dog's bones' as several dogs because the things are plural (read step message).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagplposs is built on the 'owner word first' procedure for plural owners: owners drawn as figures to count before naming, an apostrophe tile dropped into one of the letter gaps of girls/teachers/babies with a message that names the word the wrong gap makes (girl's = one), ending tiles 's / ' / s' for plurals with no s, and reading the owner count back from where the mark sits. flagposs (lesson 408) is singular owners only (dog's bone, plain plural vs 's) and flagirrplural forms plurals without any possessive; gate lab_distinct is under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the rule from the feedback before the text states it: dropping the mark before the final s of girls returns 'That makes girl's, which means one. The owner word is girls'; dropping it after the whole word of cat produces cat's while after girls it produces girls' with 'no extra s is added', so the same action gives two spellings and the learner sees why. The read step then reverses the procedure (everything before the mark is the owner word), and proofreading applies it to whole sentences.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions, each with the tempting wrong option the lab later disproves: "the girl's bags" for three girls (the count step rejects it and names the count), "teacher's" as the place for the mark in teachers (the drop step shows that gap makes one teacher), and "the childrens' toys" (the ending step's s' tile is rejected because there is no word childrens). The completion line repeats the learner's locked-in pick through A.reveal.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five challenge questions with ten distinct wrong-answer messages, each naming the slip: dog's for many dogs, a missing mark (the dogs kennel), the invented womens', women' without s, reading boys' as one boy, reading the mark as a label, apple's and apples' on a plain plural, the invented mices', and mouse's for many mice. Every step's wrong-tap message on the canvas also names what the learner's answer would mean.

readability.evidence: learn/readability.py: kid FK grade 0.6 (family limit 5.0) and adult 4.7 (limit 10.0). Kid paragraphs use one- and two-clause sentences with a worked phrase each (the dogs' kennel, the children's toys); the canvas prompts are short ('Drag the ' into a gap', 'Tap one owner or more than one owner'). The terms possessive apostrophe and plural form stay in the adult text.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph teaches one move (plural owner after s, owner word first, plurals with no s, reading back); the adult text gives the curriculum rule verbatim in substance, the two-step procedure, five named mistakes with examples and what the lab does. The content gate found no filler phrases and the explanation is under 12% the same as every other lesson, including 408 and 765.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android screenshots in light and dark for all six steps and for wrong-answer states (count step, drop step after splitting girls, ending step after children', read step after choosing more than one for dog's, proofreading after tapping 'three'). Owner figures, letter tiles and the 60 px apostrophe tile fit without clipping, feedback wraps inside the canvas at 14 px, and the error colour switches to #fda4af on the dark canvas for contrast. The walkthrough passed on iPhone 13.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button under the canvas: the two phrases in the count step, one button per gap with labels such as 'Apostrophe after girl, before s' and 'Apostrophe after the whole word girls', the three endings ('Write children's'), one owner / more than one owner, and one button per word labelled 'The word boy's has the mistake'. The canvas aria-label is rewritten with each feedback message, challenge feedback is a role=status live region, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
